🚀 8 AI Transformation Priorities

Priority 1

AI-Assisted Script Coverage & Reading

NLP script coverage for development slates — draft reports flagging structure, market comparables and budget risk; before: manual reader coverage (weeks); after: AI first-pass with script-editor sign-off

Priority 2

Production Finance Modelling

AI scenario modelling for co-finance structures, recoupment waterfalls and cash-flow projections; before: spreadsheet-dependent estimates; after: AI financial-modelling with producer validation

Priority 3

Location & Permit Intelligence

AI-mapped location database with filming-permit risk flags, access constraints and visual references; before: fragmented council processes; after: AI-indexed national location engine

Priority 4

Audience & Market Intelligence

AI aggregation of box-office, SVOD commissioning and audience data to inform development decisions; before: static market reports; after: AI live market dashboards

Priority 5

Crew Skills Gap Forecasting

ML forecasting of crew-grade shortages across departments by production volume; before: periodic surveys; after: AI workforce planning for ScreenSkills training investment

Priority 6

Archive & Rights Management

AI metadata tagging and rights-tracking for funded productions, music clearances and archive material; before: manual rights logs; after: AI-assisted chain-of-title verification

Priority 7

Inclusive Casting & Representation Monitoring

AI monitoring of funded productions against diversity and representation commitments (with human judgement on creative merit); before: post-hoc reporting; after: AI dashboards with commissioning oversight

Priority 8

Carbon Footprint of Production

AI estimation of production carbon footprints (albert-style calculators) with reduction planning; before: manual calculators; after: AI green-production planning

🚫 6 Red Lines — Legislation Backbone

Statutory Framework: Public Services Reform (Scotland) Act 2010 / Scotland Act 1998 / National Lottery etc. Act 1993 / DPA 2018 + UK GDPR / Equality Act 2010

  • NO AI-sole funding decision (all Screen Scotland award decisions require human assessment of creative merit and due process — AI assists, never determines)
  • NO AI training on copyright-protected creative works without rightsholder consent (UK CDPA 1988 + EU AI Act Article 53 transparency obligations for general-purpose AI models)
  • NO processing of children's data in screen-sector programmes without UK GDPR Article 8 consent mechanisms and age-appropriate design (Children and Young People (Scotland) Act 2014)
  • NO AI-generated content presented as Scottish cultural output without clear human authorship and labelling (protects screen-sector provenance and Creative Scotland's cultural mission)
  • NO automated discrimination in talent or crew selection (Equality Act 2010 protected characteristics — algorithmic fairness audits mandatory)
  • NO cross-border data transfer of production finance or creative IP outside UK/EEA adequacy arrangements (DPA 2018 Part 3 + UK GDPR Chapter V)
